scheme_name: Maintenance Of Pregnant Desi Indigenous Cows Ration For BPL Families
description:
The "Maintenance of Pregnant Desi Indigenous Cows Ration for BPL Families" scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to support Below Poverty Line (BPL) families engaged in dairy farming.

This scheme was officially launched on 1st April 2021 under the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to BPL families for the maintenance of pregnant indigenous cows.

The scheme aims to enhance the livelihood of these families by ensuring that they have the necessary resources to care for their livestock.

The targeted beneficiaries of this scheme are specifically BPL families who own indigenous cows.

The scheme focuses on pregnant cows as they are crucial for milk production and the overall economic stability of dairy farmers.

Under this scheme, each eligible family receives a monthly financial assistance of ₹1,000.

This amount is intended to cover the cost of feed and other necessary maintenance expenses for the pregnant cows.

The scheme is expected to benefit approximately 1 million BPL families across India.

The total budget allocated for this scheme is ₹1,200 crores for the financial year 2021-2022.

To be eligible for this scheme, applicants must belong to BPL families as defined by the Government of India.

The BPL criteria are determined based on the socio-economic caste census conducted in 2011.

Applicants must also own at least one pregnant indigenous cow to qualify for the benefits.

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme.

The application process for the scheme is straightforward and involves several key steps.

Interested applicants must first visit the official website of the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

They need to download the application form available on the website.

The completed application form must be submitted to the local veterinary office or the district animal husbandry department.

Applicants are required to provide certain documents along with their application.

These documents typically include proof of BPL status such as a BPL ration card.

They must also provide proof of ownership of the pregnant indigenous cow.

Other necessary documents may include identity proof and address proof.

Once the application is submitted, it will be verified by the local authorities.

The verification process is expected to take approximately 15 days.

After successful verification, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the bank account of the beneficiary.

The disbursement is done on a monthly basis.

The first disbursement is usually made within one month of the application approval.

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying at the central level.

At the state level, the scheme is managed by the respective state animal husbandry departments.

Each state has its own designated officers responsible for overseeing the implementation of the scheme.

The contact details for the Ministry of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on their official website.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote indigenous breeds of cattle.

Indigenous cows are known for their adaptability to local conditions and their ability to produce high-quality milk.

The government aims to increase the population of indigenous cows through this scheme.

This initiative also aligns with the government's goal of promoting sustainable agriculture and rural development.

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the dairy sector.

Many beneficiaries have reported improved livelihoods due to the financial assistance provided.

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall increase in milk production in the country.

India is one of the largest producers of milk in the world.

The dairy sector plays a significant role in the Indian economy.

It contributes approximately 4.6% to the national GDP.

The government is committed to enhancing the income of dairy farmers through various welfare schemes.

The Maintenance of Pregnant Desi Indigenous Cows Ration for BPL Families scheme is one such initiative.

It is designed to empower rural families and improve their economic conditions.

The scheme also promotes the welfare of animals by ensuring that pregnant cows receive proper care and nutrition.

The government has set a target to increase the number of beneficiaries under this scheme by 20% in the next financial year.

Regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted to assess its impact.

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account for future improvements.

The scheme is part of the larger National Dairy Plan which aims to increase milk production.

The National Dairy Plan was launched in 2012 and focuses on enhancing productivity.

The plan also aims to provide better access to markets for dairy farmers.

The Maintenance of Pregnant Desi Indigenous Cows Ration for BPL Families scheme complements these broader objectives.

It is a step towards ensuring food security and improving nutrition in rural areas.

The scheme is expected to have a multiplier effect on the rural economy.

By supporting BPL families, the scheme contributes to poverty alleviation.

The government is also working on awareness programs to educate farmers about the benefits of maintaining indigenous cows.

These programs aim to encourage more families to participate in the scheme.

Overall, the Maintenance of Pregnant Desi Indigenous Cows Ration for BPL Families scheme is a significant step towards enhancing the livelihoods of rural families.

It reflects the government's commitment to supporting the agricultural and dairy sectors in India.
